correctness.rationale: The signed face trace counts complete automorphism vertex orbits and reduces to an exact independence polynomial of the orbit graph at -1. Rotations reduce to GP(gcd(n,a),2), with four checked small exceptions; published nonequivariant homology gives the Euler evaluation. Reflection orbit graphs admit explicit strip decompositions with all nonbulk edges confined to two columns at each end. The defined eight-state transfer satisfies T^4(T^5+I)=0 by direct integer multiplication; therefore the reflection signed sums flip after n increases by ten, beyond the finite cap threshold. Exact seed evaluation completes the all-parameter claim. The degree shifts by six, so the 20-periodic character follows. Rational invariants equal quotient rational cohomology for finite simplicial group actions. The included standard-library checker reproduces the identities, boundary orbit graphs, finite seeds, further cases and quotient ranks; its finite cases only corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: The source Kim 2026-11-17 determines the all-n nonequivariant sphere-wedge homotopy type but not equivariant characters; Pandey 2026-01-05 provides independence-polynomial transfer methods but no equivariant topology. Earlier published indexed computations cover only GP(7,2) and GP(9,2), whereas this proves full all-n rotation/reflection characters. The strongest matched published result has exactly the same character, but for a different no-four-run complex on n rather than 2n vertices; it gives no stated equivariant reduction to the generalized Petersen independence complex. Independent signed orbit graphs and an eight-state matrix prove the new family character directly. This is original at best knowledge, with an explicit residual risk of an unlocated equivariant reduction.

value.rationale: Determining an entire dihedral representation over every n, and the exact rational cohomology threshold for ordinary geometric quotients, is a natural structural refinement of the previously known non-equivariant wedge ranks of a classical cubic graph family. Different reflections can act oppositely despite identical Betti numbers; the answer has 20-periodic genuinely equivariant content. The agreement with the character of a distinct no-four-run cycle complex is a nontrivial comparison between natural topological constructions, not merely a single finite numerical invariant.
